title: Session 2 — Participant 9 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Compose a main theme for an MMORPG
context: This goal will allow me to evaluate how AI can directly influence and help when working on a very creative area like music composition. The plan is to make a main theme for an MMORPG video game based on fantasy and on an existing game called Ultima Online. I plan to compose music using Claude in each step of the process.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude surprised me a lot with it’s capabilities for this specific area of the job. Composition is a very complex process that requires both a deep understanding of music and also a very creative mind, at least for humans that is. Claude was able to deliver surprising results which, although it was not fully capable of doing everything, it basically composed itself.

Step 1.step_name: Understand the plan and create a workflow
Step 1.step_action: Claude must understand what needs to be done in order to achieve a general goal. It must comprehend the analysis of the project and also suggest ideas on how to help

nodes.label: Frame the MMORPG scoring project and constrain instrument use
nodes.detail: Opens a new Claude chat, explains he is scoring 'Fragments of Chaos,' a top-down fantasy MMORPG heavily inspired by Ultima Online, and states his job is to compose the music, starting with an instrument palette. Attaches a screenshot of his VST plugin browser with an explicit instruction to use ONLY the VSTs shown.

nodes.label: Lay out palette, confirm direction, and ask what to tackle first
nodes.detail: Claude reviews the uploaded VST list, identifies its orchestral depth and folk/texture tools, sketches a palette suited to Ultima Online's medieval-fantasy world, surfaces a quick-reply asking for the score's sonic direction, then — once the user confirms fully orchestral/classic MMO — affirms the choice and asks which piece of the project to tackle first.

nodes.label: Select the fully-orchestral direction and choose the main theme as the starting focus
nodes.detail: Chooses 'Fully orchestral/classic MMO' from the quick-reply options, explains that this matches the old MMO that inspired the game and deliberately rules out folk or synth elements, then decides to start with the main theme since it hasn't been worked on yet, setting the agenda for the rest of the session.

nodes.label: Deliver a function-organized instrument palette
nodes.detail: Lays out a working palette by role: 'Originals - Epic Strings' for the main theme/hero statement, Bohemian Violin or Cello for an intimate secondary phrase/countermelody, 'Originals - Intimate Grand Piano' to open the theme solo, Appassionata Strings for climax thickness, and Epic Choir plus Cinematic Percussion for the final statement, also suggesting the Vienna Synchron Player.

nodes.label: Read Claude's working palette

Step 2.step_name: Create a palette of instruments for the theme proposed
Step 2.step_action: Claude must suggest a palette of instruments from my VST library to create the suggested track.

nodes.label: Select Bohemian Cello over Violin for the secondary voice
nodes.detail: Picks Bohemian Cello rather than Violin for the intimate secondary phrase/countermelody role.

nodes.label: Independently justify the Cello choice with tonal reasoning
nodes.detail: Unprompted, explains that Bohemian Cello carries a warmer, more human, and vulnerable quality than Violin for this role, which pleasantly surprises the participant since he did not ask for justification.

nodes.label: Push back on the ambiguous Vienna Synchron Player suggestion
nodes.detail: Notes that Synchron Player is a large multi-instrument bundle and Claude can't know which specific bundled instruments he actually owns; clarifies his context so Claude can narrow it down correctly.

nodes.label: Correctly identify the free-tier pack and settle on Celestial Strings
nodes.detail: Recognizes the participant's owned instrument set is the free-tier 'HELLO' pack bundled with the player, and the two settle on Celestial Strings as the specific patch to use.

nodes.label: Wire the recommended instruments into FL Studio
nodes.detail: In parallel, off-chat, opens FL Studio and begins loading the recommended instruments (Epic Strings, Bohemian Cello, Intimate Grand Piano, Sampler, Vienna Synchron Player) as channel-rack/mixer tracks.

Step 3.step_name: Suggestions for key, tempo and musical theory specifics
Step 3.step_action: Ask Claude to suggest a key, tempo, time signature, and harmonic/melodic approach appropriate to the fantasy MMORPG theme

nodes.label: Ask Claude to challenge itself on tempo and time signature
nodes.detail: Once the instruments are added in FL Studio, asks Claude to 'challenge itself more' and propose a tempo and time signature rather than defer the decision back to him.

nodes.label: Suggest a loop-friendly tempo of 72-76 BPM
nodes.detail: Recommends a tempo range typical of classic-MMO main themes, framed as loop-friendly for a piece meant to hold up over hundreds of hours of repeat listening.

nodes.label: Critique the tempo suggestion on camera as generic
nodes.detail: Reacts to camera that the 72-76 BPM range feels like a generic default rather than something derived from deeper knowledge of the specific game, wishing Claude had asked more before settling on a number.

nodes.label: Ask whether rubato is allowed in the solo intro
nodes.detail: Follows up asking whether rubato (flexible expressive timing) is permitted for the solo intro instrument — rendered in the raw ASR transcript as the garbled 'Hey, Sandy, or was Roboto allowed,' corrected here against the video and workflow doc.

nodes.label: Recommend 4/4 time and D minor with emotionally-grounded reasoning
nodes.detail: Suggests 4/4 time (which the participant agrees is simple and fits a main theme) and D minor, relative to F major, explaining the key as 'noble and melancholic' and idiomatic for fantasy scoring; the participant calls this 'a good analysis,' impressed the reasoning ties to the emotional target rather than being arbitrary.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about recommending 4/4 time and D minor with emotionally-grounded reasoning

Step 4.step_name: Generation of MIDI files for distinct instruments
Step 4.step_action: Have Claude generate MIDI patterns for each instrument in the palette, based on the key, tempo, and theory direction from Step 3, to import directly into FL Studio.

nodes.label: Self-direct a harder test: real CC1 mod-wheel automation
nodes.detail: Pushes into a self-directed extension of MIDI generation, asking Claude to write genuine CC1 (mod-wheel) automation for Klevgrand's 'Guiro' instrument (spoken as 'Guido,' an ASR mishearing of the plugin's actual on-screen name), since its expression is driven by continuous mod-wheel movement on a held gate note rather than note velocity.

nodes.label: Write and export CC1 automation code
nodes.detail: Writes code explicitly targeting MIDI control=1, verifies the generated file has real gate-note content, and exports 'fragments_guiro_texture.mid,' reporting 51 embedded CC1 messages.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about writing and exporting CC1 automation code
Test the sound
Import the file and find no CC automation came through
nodes.detail: Imports the file into FL Studio and reports back that the CC data did not write onto the MIDI file — only the note events are visible.

nodes.label: Ask for CC rather than CC1
Re-verify the CC1 data is genuinely present in the exported file
nodes.detail: Rather than assume the export worked, runs code to directly re-read the saved file from disk and confirms 51 CC1 messages are genuinely present on channel 0 (channel 1 in FL's 1-indexed display), establishing the export itself is correct.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about re-verifying the CC1 data is genuinely present in the exported file
Confirm FL Studio's piano roll shows notes but zero automation
nodes.detail: Reports seeing only the two gate notes in FL Studio's piano roll, with no automation writing into any CC lane, despite the confirmed presence of the data on disk.

nodes.label: Identify FL Studio's split note/CC import as the root cause
nodes.detail: Web-searches the issue and finds that FL Studio treats importing notes and importing controller/CC data as two entirely separate operations — the piano roll's standard MIDI import only handles notes — explaining exactly why notes came in but CC1 did not.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about identifying FL Studio's split note/CC import as the root cause
Screenshot the correctly-targeted but flat CC1 control lane
nodes.detail: Follows Claude's suggestion to check the Event Editor / control lane route, confirms the lane is set to 'MIDI CC #1 (Modulation wheel)' — the right lane — but sends a screenshot showing it is completely flat.

nodes.label: Conclude the gap is FL Studio's import behavior, not generation
nodes.detail: Confirms the correct lane is selected but genuinely empty, concluding this is an FL Studio MIDI-import limitation rather than a flaw in what Claude generated, and suggests skipping file-import for CC data entirely in favor of drawing the scratch curve by hand.

nodes.label: Search on Google
Hand-draw the CC1 curve to demonstrate the target expression
nodes.detail: Manually records/draws the CC1 mod-wheel curve on the Guiro channel to show what the automation should look like, then repeats the demonstration on Bohemian Cello and Appassionata Strings, explicitly contrasting this fine-grained mod-wheel control against the coarser note-velocity control Claude used elsewhere in the session.

Step 5.step_action: Ask Claude for a mixing approach for the composed theme, covering EQ, panning, reverb, and levels to balance the instrument palette into a cohesive mix.

nodes.label: Share the full plugin database and ask for a mixing plan
nodes.detail: Gives Claude his complete mixing/mastering toolkit — iZotope's RX 11 and Ozone 12 suites, Kush Clariphonic/CLA, Kilohearts utility plugins, ValhallaRoom, and specialty tools — and asks which to use to mix and master the track.

nodes.label: Propose a practical, instrument-by-instrument signal chain
nodes.detail: Rather than listing every plugin, proposes EQ before compression, a high-pass/low-end rolloff, a notch around 300-500Hz to remove boxiness, glue compression, a shared ValhallaRoom reverb bus for spatial cohesion, and Ozone's Imager/Stereo Eyes for width — sequenced melody first, then countermelody/underlay, then bass/harmony, then percussion.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about proposing a practical, instrument-by-instrument signal chain
Ask for a step by step guidance
Generate a guidance
Implement the chain on the melody insert in FL Studio's mixer
nodes.detail: Builds the recommended chain (kHs Compressor, Ozone 12 Dynamic EQ) on the melody's mixer insert, starting with the main Epic Strings theme statement.

nodes.label: Extend the chain to countermelody, bass, and harmony layers
nodes.detail: Continues applying the mixing chain to the countermelody/underlay tracks and then the foundational bass/harmony layer, agreeing with Claude's low-end-focus and high-mid-boost suggestions for the bass.

nodes.label: Mix percussion and override a panning suggestion
nodes.detail: Applies the shared ValhallaRoom reverb-bus idea to percussion, but overrides Claude's suggestion to use 'Placeit' for panning, judging it's built for true spatial/room placement rather than simple left-right positioning; observes that Claude tends to spread the mix across more plugins than strictly necessary.

custom-1.step_action: Close out the session with a spoken summary reflecting on Claude's overall composition performance and remaining limitations.

nodes.label: Export the finished FL Studio project
nodes.detail: Wraps up the hands-on work by exporting the finished FL Studio project file.

nodes.label: Deliver a spoken wrap-up reflection on the session
nodes.detail: Reflects to camera that the session went well: impressed that Claude chose the instruments, generated essentially the entire composition, and guided the mixing/mastering — 'pretty impressive' for something not made by a human composer. Reiterates CC automation as the one meaningful capability gap, noting it would be 'revolutionary' for composers if solved, and mentions an unsuccessful attempt to get an MCP server working for direct DAW control, speculating it may be a Mac-specific issue. Closes with one more manual demonstration of recording a CC/mod-wheel movement by hand.

Step 1.step_name: Understand the plan and create a workflow
Step 1.step_action: Claude must understand what needs to be done in order to achieve a general goal. It must comprehend the analysis of the project and also suggest ideas on how to help
Step 1.output: Textual delivery and planning for the project.
rubrics: A score of 5 means Claude understood the creative brief
A score of 5 means Claude proposed a clear workflow that breaks the process into logical steps
A score of 5 means the plan considered the specific creative constraints of the project, rather than a general suggestion
A score of 5 means Claude asked relevant clarifying questions or flagged missing information, instead of suggesting made up information about the project
A score of 5 means the output was ready to act on immediately, without needing another prompt to make it usable

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude did a good job understanding the project, suggesting what we could work on, asking which type of game it is and asking which reference would be a good idea to base ourselves off of. I did however have to clarify a few details with another prompt to correct it.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It created a workflow with the correct understanding of the project, suggesting what could be worked on and asking further questions for its own research.

Step 2.step_name: Create a palette of instruments for the theme proposed
Step 2.step_action: Claude must suggest a palette of instruments from my VST library to create the suggested track.
Step 2.output: A list of which instruments should be used and what to use them for
rubrics: A score of 5 means Claude correctly identified the instruments available in the screenshot of my VST library, without suggesting instruments I don't own
A score of 5 means the assigned roles per instrument (melody, harmony and percussion) fit the fantasy/MMORPG tone from Step 1
A score of 5 means the palette accounts for how the instruments sit together in a mix, avoiding suggestions that would clash
A score of 5 means the recommendations reference the actual plugin/library name rather than a generic instrument
A score of 5 means the palette is appropriately sized for a main theme, not overloaded with more instruments than it needs

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude correctly identified the VST libraries, gave the palette suggestion which I agreed with completely and gave me a full list with the library names. It did not however account for the fact that some libraries are just that, libraries containing many instruments. For some, it did not pick the unique instrument inside the library, rather, it just suggested the library as a whole.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude delivered a good and accurate list of vsts to use with the exclusion of a library that had a varied amount of instruments, which it did not identify and pick one.

Step 3.step_name: Suggestions for key, tempo and musical theory specifics
Step 3.step_action: Ask Claude to suggest a key, tempo, time signature, and harmonic/melodic approach appropriate to the fantasy MMORPG theme
Step 3.output: A written recommendation of key, tempo, time signature, and melodic ideas
rubrics: A score of 5 means the key, tempo, and time signature genuinely cause the fantasy/MMORPG feel from the brief, not a generic default used for cinema
A score of 5 means Claude explains the music theory reasoning behind each choice rather than just stating it
A score of 5 means the suggested progressions are specific enough to input directly into FL Studio without any more interpretation
A score of 5 means the theory suggestions stay consistent with the Step 2 instrument palette
A score of 5 means the recommendation ties back to the Ultima Online inspiration

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude gave good ideas and explained them really well without issue. I also noticed that it was analyzing older MMORPG’s and their tracks for inspiration on what to do. The only point missing was from it not being ready for direct implementation for FL Studio

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully analyzed the project and gave good ideas for music theory which fit the style I was looking for, analyzing the inspirations for the score.

Step 4.step_name: Generation of MIDI files for distinct instruments
Step 4.step_action: Have Claude generate MIDI patterns for each instrument in the palette, based on the key, tempo, and theory direction from Step 3, to import directly into FL Studio.
Step 4.output: MIDI files for each instrument part
rubrics: A score of 5 means the generated MIDI is musically coherent on its own, with a clear melodic or harmonic idea rather than random notes
A score of 5 means the parts for different instruments work together without clashing when played back simultaneously
A score of 5 means the MIDI respects the key, tempo, and theory decisions from Step 3 without deviating
A score of 5 means the note ranges and voicings fit each instrument
A score of 5 means the MIDI files import into FL Studio cleanly and are ready to route to the assigned instrument

ratings.output_quality_reason: Even though I gave it a three, I believe Claude did really well in this section. It surpassed my expectations with its delivery. Claude did not get a 5 because some notes were out of tune, but overall, it’s delivery was well thought out and the MIDI file was easy to drag in.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude successfully delivered MIDI files for each instrument that had been stated and fitted to the role assigned to each instrument (Melody, harmony, bass, etc.) forming a coherent track that worked well together (excluding one part which was out of tune)

Step 5.step_action: Ask Claude for a mixing approach for the composed theme, covering EQ, panning, reverb, and levels to balance the instrument palette into a cohesive mix.
Step 5.output: A step by step mixing guide with specific plugin/parameter suggestions per instrument
rubrics: A score of 5 means the mixing guide results in a balanced mix where every instrument is audible and none is buried
A score of 5 means the guide specifies exact values instead of vague concepts
A score of 5 means the panning and spatial suggestions create a sense of width and depth
A score of 5 means the guide is specific to plugins available in my FL Studio rather than generic mixing theory
A score of 5 means the resulting mix sounds comparable in quality to a professionally produced game theme

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude did in fact use most of my plugins and suggested good general ideas, but it lacked specifics and didn’t reach a professional mix. It also tried using many plugins for variety, which was not very efficient.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It did mix the track and produced a good composition overall, but it was lacking in details both on the workflow and on the actual mix.
